title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hook with metric-based quality gating
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We need a CI-level guard that runs the eval-harness prompt-set regression suite on PRs touching the serving runtime, prompt assets, or any code that influences generation. Motivation: prevent accidental quality regressions by failing merges when key eval metrics (e.g., exact-match, BLEU-like rerank NDCG, and hallucination rate) regress beyond configurable thresholds. This PR adds a reusable GitHub Actions job and a small hook that runs a lightweight eval subset on PRs and reports metric deltas to Slack and the PR page.

What this change does: adds a new workflow eval-harness/.github/workflows/prompt-regression.yml that triggers on pull_request for affected paths; implements eval-harness/hooks/prompt_regression_hook.py which loads the configured prompt sets, runs the eval runner with cached model artifacts, computes metrics and compares against baseline thresholds stored in eval-harness/eval/metrics/thresholds.yaml; fails the job if any metric crosses the regression delta; posts a summary comment on the PR and emits structured results to the CI artifact store. Adds unit tests and a small e2e job to avoid flakes.

Testing and validation: unit tests added in eval-harness/tests/test_prompt_regression.py covering threshold logic, result serialization, and Slack/PR reporting mocks. e2e job run on canary branch with a small prompt subset to verify runtime, caching, and CI artifact upload. Local test plan: run the hook against a recorded baseline (tests/fixtures) and assert no false positives on metric noise.

Checklist: - [x] Add ci workflow and hook implementation. - [x] Add thresholds file and sane defaults. - [x] Unit and integration tests. - [x] Docs update explaining configuration and how to opt out for long-running experiments. - [x] Post-merge alerting to #model-quality slack channel.

Notes on backwards compatibility and ops: thresholds.yaml is intended to be tuned per-model and lives in the repo; ops can override via REDWOOD_EVAL_THRESHOLD_URL. The job is opt-in for now via paths filter; we will expand coverage after monitoring for false positives.

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Can we make the default thresholds conservative to avoid noisy failures? Suggested +3% absolute on recall-like metrics as a starting point.
Author (Aisha): Agreed. I set conservative defaults in thresholds.yaml and added instructions for teams to override per-model. Also added a noise-tolerant comparison in the hook.
Liam O'Connor: The reporting comment is large; can we upload full JSON to CI artifacts and keep the PR comment summary short?
Author (Aisha): Updated to attach full results as a CI artifact and keep the PR comment to a one-line status with a link to the artifact.
Sofia Martinez: Please add unit tests that simulate metric drift but within epsilon to assert no false positives.
Author (Aisha): Added tests covering epsilon and flaky-run aggregation logic.
release_notes: Add opt-in CI hook that runs prompt-set regression checks and enforces metric-based quality gates. Configurable thresholds per model and Slack/PR notifications. Defaults are conservative to minimize false positives.
notes: Monitored for 48 hours post-merge. No regressions triggered in follow-up canary runs. Team to consider enabling path filters for broader set of changes after 2 weeks.
